ap_chemistry-m01.stem: A rigid $4\text{ L}$ flask holds $\mathrm{Ar}$(g) at $2\text{ atm}$, and a second rigid $1\text{ L}$ flask holds $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$(g) at $1.5\text{ atm}$. Both flasks are at $273\text{ K}$ and are joined by a tube with a closed stopcock. The stopcock is opened and the gases mix while the temperature stays at $273\text{ K}$. Assuming ideal behavior and no reaction, what is the final total pressure in the connected flasks, in atm?

options.why: At constant T each gas keeps its amount, n = PV/RT, so n_total = (P1V1 + P2V2)/RT and P_final = n_total RT/(V1 + V2) = ((2)(4) + (1.5)(1))/(4 + 1) = 1.90 atm.
Divides the sum of the two pressures by the combined volume.
Divides only the first gas's PV by the combined volume and ignores the second gas.
